text:
Maya Patel: FYI ran the FP8 canary on atlas-13B (L40S pool) and seeing small but consistent degradation on long-context evals (>=4k). perplexity +0.8% vs fp16 baseline.
Rui Zhang: can you paste the canary config? batch sizes, seq len distribution?
Maya Patel: config:
```
model: atlas-13b
precision: fp8
kernel: h100-optimized? no, l40s-tiling
batching: dynamic
seq_lengths: [512, 1024, 2048, 4096, 8192]
canary_pct: 2%
```
Maya Patel: note: we forced mixed-precision handshake on L40S (fp8 main + fp16 fallback for kv convs). logs attached in S3.
Dmitri Volkov: @Maya can you attach the run traces? I want the kernel fallback histogram and any NaN/inf counts. FP8 on L40S sometimes hits activation saturation for long prefixes.
Maya Patel: upload: s3://redwood-canaries/atlas13b/1754129876/traces.tar.gz
Sasha Klein: quick question — are we using per-channel scaling (AWQ-like) or symmetric per-tensor scales? That changes saturation behavior.
Maya Patel: AWQ-ish per-channel by default, but we had a compatibility shim to fall back to per-tensor for some legacy kernels.
Ankit Rao: which shim? I remember a heuristic that forces per-tensor on layers with <64 channels; that can shift distribution.
Rui Zhang: this is interesting: on H100 fp8 canary we saw negligible delta, so this seems platform-specific (L40S tiling + kernel handshake). Could be tiling mismatch for large seqs.
Dmitri Volkov: +1. On L40S our tiling splits attention into uneven chunks; scale recomputation across tile boundary can accumulate error. If KV cache alignment differs for longer prefixes, numeric drift shows up.
Sasha Klein: we should check two hypotheses: (1) activation clipping from quant scale mismatch at layer boundaries, (2) unexpected fallback to fp32 for some matmuls due to autotuner mismatch.
Maya Patel: I ran a micro-bench with deterministic seeds and a single long sequence (8192). Observed small spikes in layer7 activation max (~1.2x) vs H100 run.
Dmitri Volkov: can you paste the relevant excerpt from the kernel trace? specifically lines showing "tile_end_scale_update" and "fallback_reason"
Maya Patel: excerpt:
```
[1754129883] tile0: max_act=0.842
[1754129884] tile1: max_act=1.02
[1754129885] tile2: tile_end_scale_update: scale_old=0.03125 scale_new=0.0285
[1754129885] kernel: fallback_reason=tile_overlap_residual
[1754129886] tile3: max_act=1.13
```
Ankit Rao: fallback_reason=tile_overlap_residual is the new guard for overlap compensation. If that triggers, we recompute scales which can perturb quantization. For long sequences many tiles trigger it.
Rui Zhang: any difference in batch sizes between H100 and L40S runs? A higher batch results in different effective normalization.
Maya Patel: both runs used batch=1 for longseq canary.
Sasha Klein: mitigation ideas: (A) disable the overlap_residual guard for canary to measure effect, (B) enable per-layer recalibration (recompute scales with running stats from longer prefix), (C) try AWQ->GPTQ quant config to see if symmetric scales help.
Dmitri Volkov: I want to stress that wrong fix can hide a real model-quality regression. Let's do controlled AB tests: replicate identical input seeds on both runtimes, log token-level divergences and probability deltas.
Maya Patel: agreed. Plan: 1) rerun deterministic longseq canary with guard disabled (rollout flag: enable.tile_overlap_guard=false) 2) run per-layer recalibration pass (flag: quant.recalibrate_per_layer=true) 3) run GPTQ-style quant on a small subset and compare. Will post results by EOD.
build-bot: Canary run scheduled: job-id=canary-1754129876-2, expected finish ~1754133000
Ankit Rao: also add telemetry to capture "scale_jump_count" per-layer and "fallback_count" per-request so we can correlate with QA deltas.
Rui Zhang: if disabling guard removes delta, maybe we need a smoother scale interpolation instead of abrupt recompute. We should prototype linear interpolation between old/new scales across tile boundaries.
Sasha Klein: +1. Also check optimizer kernels — some MatMul variants on L40S are using vectorized half-paths that interact poorly with per-channel scales.
Maya Patel: thanks all — I'll run the three experiments and upload logs. If anyone wants access to the canary job, ping me and I'll give the IAM link.
Dmitri Volkov: thanks @Maya. If the per-layer recalibration works, we should consider adding it as an optional safety for L40S fp8 until kernel handshake matures.
Maya Patel: noted. I'll include rollout recommendation in the results: (a) hold canary, (b) disable guard if safe for short term, (c) enable recalibration as medium-term.
Sasha Klein: great. small ask: include a few sample prompts where token-level probs deviate >1e-3 so evals-team can inspect semantics.
Maya Patel: will do.
Rui Zhang: thanks team. follow-ups in #eng-ml on the same thread. :thumbsup:
